raw_response:
I will keep my land arrangement simple and labor-saving. Because my household has only part of its labor available for farming, and I have reliable well irrigation, I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation and keep a smaller block in cotton. That matches what I already know how to manage, spreads risk across grain and cash crops, and fits my 25 years of experience. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it gives me stable emergence and yield, and I will avoid overly aggressive input use because I care more about steady output than gambling on a very high harvest. On the wheat-maize land, I will push for stable grain production with moderate fertilizer, timely irrigation, and basic pest control. On cotton, I will keep the area smaller because it needs more management and pesticide work, but I still want some cash income from it. I will use simpler tillage where I can to save time, but I will prepare the cotton ground more carefully because stand establishment matters there.
